name: Sorank
tagline: SEO tool built around a link exchange network, where member sites trade backlinks with each other.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software half of a link exchange platform is boring: a directory of sites, some metrics, a matching queue, an email thread, a checker that confirms the link went live. An agent can build all of that in a weekend. What it cannot build is the other side of the exchange: thousands of site owners who already signed up, already have domains with some authority, and are already willing to place a link for you. A link network with one member is a spreadsheet. If you want the DIY version, build the part that is actually yours: tracking, verifying and auditing the backlinks you get from anywhere, including the ones you negotiated by hand.
coreLoopDIY: A local backlink tracker that stores your target links, crawls each linking page on a schedule, and tells you when a link disappears, goes nofollow, or changes anchor text.
requirements: Node 20 and a local SQLite file
Outbound HTTP access to crawl third-party pages politely
Your own list of linking pages to monitor
Optional: an SMTP or webhook target for alerts
whatYouLose: The actual network: a pool of other site owners willing to link to you
Any matching or reciprocity logic that only works with many participants
Whatever authority metrics they license or compute across their member graph
Reputational filtering, so you get to judge link quality yourself
Nobody to blame when a link partner ghosts you
moatNotes: Two-sided by construction: every member is both a buyer and a seller of link placements, so value scales with headcount and dies without it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because link building is a supply problem, not a software problem. Finding someone who owns a real site, in a vaguely related niche, who will put your URL on a page that search engines already crawl, is the entire difficulty. A platform that has already collected those people sells you access to supply, and the dashboard around it is packaging. Whether that supply is worth paying for, or whether it is a self-referential link farm that gets discounted the moment a search engine notices the pattern, is a separate and much less comfortable question.
notes: The dashboard is a weekend; the membership roll is not. The moat is a two-sided pool of site owners willing to trade links, which is worth exactly as much as its headcount.
prompt:
Build a local backlink monitor called linkwatch. Single Node 20 + TypeScript project, no framework beyond what is listed.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- TypeScript, Node 20, run with tsx
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/linkwatch.db
- HTTP server with Hono, serving plain server-rendered HTML plus a little vanilla JS
- undici fetch for crawling, cheerio for parsing
- node-cron for scheduling
- dotenv for secrets

Data model:
- targets: id, url (a page on my site I want links to), notes
- links: id, target_id, source_url (the page that should link to me), partner_name, expected_anchor, first_seen, last_checked, status, last_error
- checks: id, link_id, checked_at, http_status, found (bool), anchor_text, rel_attr, page_title

Core loop:
- A checker that fetches each source_url with a real user agent, respects robots.txt for that host, parses all anchors, and looks for any href matching the target url ignoring trailing slash, utm params and http vs https
- Record found/not found, the anchor text, and the rel attribute (flag nofollow, sponsored, ugc)
- Compute status per link: live, live-nofollow, anchor-changed, missing, unreachable
- Rate limit to one request per host every 5 seconds, max 3 concurrent hosts, retry once on 5xx

UI at localhost:8787:
- One table of all links with status badges, last checked, anchor text, and a filter by status
- Detail page per link showing check history
- Forms to add targets and links, plus CSV import and CSV export
- A "check now" button per link and a "check all" button

Scheduling and alerts:
- Cron job daily at 04:00 local time to check everything
- On any transition to missing, live-nofollow or anchor-changed, POST a JSON summary to WEBHOOK_URL if set in .env

Out of scope, do not build:
- No accounts, no login, no multi-tenant anything
- No hosted deployment, no telemetry, no analytics
- No third-party SEO metric APIs, no domain authority scores, no link marketplace or partner matching

Deliver: package.json scripts (dev, check, migrate), a migration that creates the schema, a seeded example row, .env.example with WEBHOOK_URL, and a README with exact run commands.
